item.title: Cervical / Upper Trapezius MFR
stabilization: Support head/shoulder so patient can relax.
contact: Broad hand/finger contact over upper trapezius/cervical fascia, avoiding anterior neck.
forceDirection: Slow longitudinal, cross-hand or indirect ease direction depending on irritability.
safety: Avoid acute vascular/neurological concern, infection or unstable injury.
item.visualCue: Broad fascial contact → Slow sustained load → Re-test neck movement.

subTechniques.name: Suboccipital Myofascial Release
subTechniques.target: Suboccipital fascia and short upper-cervical extensors
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce upper-cervical soft-tissue guarding and improve comfortable head/neck movement.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the head fully supported in neutral.
subTechniques.contact: Finger pads or knuckles rest gently beneath the occiput without pressing the anterior neck.
subTechniques.direction: Use a slow sustained traction/lift and allow the tissues to soften; direct work can gently engage the felt restriction while indirect work follows the direction of ease.
subTechniques.dosage: 60–120 seconds of sustained low-load contact, repeated only if the comparable sign improves.
subTechniques.reassess: Upper-cervical rotation, headache-related comparable sign and comfort with chin nod.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Avoid chasing a dramatic 'release' sensation; a useful change in movement or symptoms is the real outcome.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop if dizziness, unusual headache, visual symptoms or neurological change occurs.

subTechniques.name: Upper Trapezius Fascial Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve comfortable side-bending and shoulder-girdle movement when fascial tenderness/restriction is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine or sitting with the shoulder supported and neck relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Broad hand contact over the upper trapezius between shoulder and neck.
subTechniques.direction: Engage the tissue slowly in the direction of greatest restriction for direct MFR, or follow the easiest direction for indirect MFR.
subTechniques.reassess: Cervical side-bending, shoulder elevation and local pain.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Use broad contact—pinching the upper trapezius is not the same as myofascial release.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid direct pressure over the anterior/lateral neurovascular neck.
